title: 2027 Hyundai Kona Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The 2027 Hyundai Kona features some minor spec changes, but otherwise this bold-looking compact crossover is unchanged.
body_markdown:
Hyundai has built a strong lineup of crossover SUVs, from the tiny Venue to the spacious three-row Palisade. The subcompact Kona, offered with a choice of front-wheel drive (FWD) or all-wheel drive (AWD) and four trim levels, sits at the smaller end of the spectrum, offering value and versatility to rival cars such as the Kia Seltos, the Honda HR-V, the Toyota Corolla Cross, and the Volkswagen Taos.

## What’s New for the 2027 Hyundai Kona


Hyundai continues to offer four Kona trim levels: SE, SEL Sport, SEL Premium, and Limited. For 2027, ambient lighting is available only on the top trim, and the automaker's idle stop-and-go feature is not available on the SE. Otherwise, it's status quo for this second-generation subcompact crossover SUV, which debuted for the 2024 model year. Hyundai first introduced the Kona nameplate in 2018.


## Design


Despite not being die-hard Star Trek fans, the 2027 Hyundai Kona's face had us Googling the character with the horizontal band of eyeglasses. His name is Geordi La Forge, and he may just be the inspiration behind the Kona's front end. Or maybe not. Regardless, the look is unique with that strip of LED lighting, LED lights sitting low and to the outer edges of the bumper, and a substantial grille. Along the flanks of the SE are ample swaths of black cladding, generic 17-inch silver wheels, and eye-catching body lines, while the tail features a spoiler and lighting arrangement similar to the front. The SEL Sport adds black roof rails, black 18-inch alloys, and rear privacy glass. Lighter cladding and two-tone 19-inch wheels highlight the SEL Premium, while the Limited gets a touch of chrome trim and machined alloys.


## Powertrain


The 2027 Kona is available with two engine options. SE and SEL Sport trims use a 2.0-liter four-cylinder, while the SEL Premium and Limited use a 1.6-liter four-cylinder engine. The difference is that the 1.6-liter engine is turbocharged and produces 190 horsepower and 195 pound-feet of torque compared with the 2.0-liter engine’s 147 hp and 132 lb-ft. Either can be paired with FWD or AWD and selectable drive modes, though transmissions differ; a continuously variable transmission (CVT) pairs with the 2.0-liter engine, while the 1.6-liter engine gets an eight-speed automatic with paddle shifters. According to the EPA, efficiency ranges from 28 mpg city, 35 mpg highway, and 31 mpg combined for the 2.0-liter FWD configuration to 24 mpg, 29 mpg, and 26 mpg with the turbo and AWD. Hyundai recommends regular-grade gasoline for both, so the extra power doesn't require a premium at the pump.


## Interior


The interior resembles that of many current Hyundai models, with a horizontal sight line that runs nearly level from the upper door panels to the flat-top dash. Various pockets and cubbies offer ample storage, and the 60/40 folding and reclining rear bench seat can be lowered to provide 63.7 cubic feet of cargo space. With all seats upright, cargo volume is 25.5 cubic feet and seating capacity is five. The SE covers the basic creature comforts, but Hyundai dresses up the SEL Sport with a leather-wrapped steering wheel, heated front seats with dual manual height adjustment, a rear fold-down armrest, and other little touches such as illumination for the vanity mirrors. The SEL Premium adds leatherette upholstery and a power-adjustable driver's seat, while the Limited tops things off with a sunroof, ambient lighting, ventilated front seats, a heated steering wheel, a hands-free power liftgate, and more.


## Technology


The 2027 Kona has no shortage of tech features. The SE comes with a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment display, a six-speaker audio system, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, four USB ports, and Hyundai's Bluelink connected services. Buyers also get HD radio, a complimentary SiriusXM satellite radio trial, and amenities such as proximity keyless entry. Move up to the SEL Sport for dual-zone climate control and wireless charging, or go all in with a Kona Limited for a standard eight-speaker Bose audio system, a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, and remote smart-parking assist.

## Safety


Hyundai also takes a generous approach to safety equipment. All 2027 Konas come with forward-collision warning with cyclist and pedestrian detection, lane-centering and lane-keep assist, blind-spot monitors, rear cross-traffic alert, and adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go. The bounty of standard features goes on with safe-exit assist, high-beam assist, traffic-sign recognition, and a driver-attention monitor. Upper trims get parking sensors, a surround-view camera, and rear-collision warning. When subjected to National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) tests, the 2027 Kona earned an overall four-out-of-five-star rating. However, the Hyundai did not meet the NHTSA's pedestrian protection performance criteria. In Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) tests, the Kona scored a Good rating in nearly every category, prompting the IIHS to name it a 2026 Top Safety Pick+.


## Pricing and Release Date


On sale now, the 2027 Hyundai Kona fights the notion that new cars can't be affordable. At the time of writing, pricing started at $25,500 for the SE FWD, $26,825 for the SEL Sport FWD, $28,425 for the SEL Premium FWD, and $32,535 for the Limited FWD. There's also a $1,650 destination charge, while AWD costs an additional $1,500. In other words, true base prices range from $27,150 (SE FWD) to $35,685 (Limited AWD). Hyundai doesn't offer any factory option packages, though available dealer accessories cost between $20 and $390, and select exterior paint colors add $500.
